item.title: Former Saint Thomas student Nathan Hughes to make Flying Fijians debut
item.description: Former Saint Thomas High School student and former England international loose forward, Nathan Hughes is set to make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians after being named in the starting XV to face France in the 2026 Nations Championship. Hughes, who previously represented England at international level, has been handed the number 8 jersey as Fiji prepare to face France at Groupama Stadium
item.content:encoded:
Former Saint Thomas High School student and former England international loose forward, Nathan Hughes is set to make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians after being named in the starting XV to face France in the 2026 Nations Championship.

Hughes, who previously represented England at international level, has been handed the number 8 jersey as Fiji prepare to face France at Groupama Stadium in Lyon.

His inclusion adds significant experience, power and physicality to a formidable Fijian forward pack that will be expected to match France's intensity and aggression up front.

Captain Tevita Ikanivere will lead the forwards alongside Eroni Mawi, Luke Tagi, Mesake Vocevoce, Isoa Nasilasila, Pita-Gus Sowakula, Kitione Salawa and Hughes .

Meanwhile, the Flying Fijians have assembled an exciting backline featuring several players with experience in France's highly competitive Top 14 competition.

Simione Kuruvoli will start at halfback, partnering flyhalf Isikeli Rabitu, while Jiuta Wainiqolo, Vinaya Habosi, Iosefo Masi, Selestino Ravutaumada and fullback Salesi Rayasi complete the starting backline.

The Flying Fijians will also have experienced players coming off the bench, including Zuriel Togiatama, Peni Ravai, Inoke Ravuwasa, Peceli Yato, Elia Canakaivata, Frank Lomani, Ben Volavola and Sireli Maqala.

With a powerful forward pack and an explosive backline, the Flying Fijians will be determined to make their presence felt against France.

Fiji will face France at 8.10am on Sunday.

item.content:encoded:
The Australian Jillaroos are taking Fiji's Bulikula seriously ahead of their Rugby League World Cup semi-final clash, acknowledging the threat posed by the Fijian side following an impressive campaign in their debut tournament.

The Bulikula have made a strong impression at the tournament, pushing the Kiwi Ferns to the limit in their opening match before recording convincing victories over France and Papua New Guinea.

Jillaroos player Kezie Apps says the team is aware of Fiji's ability to make fast starts, having scored within the opening 10 minutes of their last two matches.

Apps says the Jillaroos have discussed Fiji's strengths and are preparing for what they expect to be a challenging encounter.

She says reaching the semi-finals brings a different level of competition and the team is not taking Fiji lightly.

Apps, who returns to the side this week after serving as the 18th player against Wales, says the pressure of defending their title is something the team views as a privilege.

She says the Jillaroos remain focused on their goal of securing a fourth consecutive World Cup title, but their immediate priority is delivering a strong performance against Fiji.

Apps says the team's theme for the week is excellence, with players focused on improving individually and collectively and making the most of every opportunity.

The Bulikula will face the Jillaroos at 6.45pm Sunday at Allianz Stadium, with a place in the Rugby League World Cup final at stake.

The match will be followed by the men's semi-final between the Australian Kangaroos and Samoa at 9.05pm.

item.title: Fiji's Grace Khelan falls just 0.23 seconds short of 50m Freestyle final
item.description: Team Fiji swimmer Grace Khelan narrowly misses out on a place in the Women's 50m Freestyle final at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, finishing just 0.23 seconds outside qualification. Khelan finishes 11th out of 68 swimmers in the heats, clocking 26.88 seconds.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji swimmer Grace Khelan narrowly misses out on a place in the Women's 50m Freestyle final at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, finishing just 0.23 seconds outside qualification.

Khelan finishes 11th out of 68 swimmers in the heats, clocking 26.88 seconds.

She also competed in the Women's 50m Butterfly, recording 29.87 seconds to finish 19th out of 40 swimmers.

Meanwhile, fellow Fiji swimmer Thaddeus Kwong finishes 23rd out of 42 competitors in the Men's 50m Butterfly, clocking 26.53 seconds.

Team Fiji's attention now turns to triathlete Josiah Croker, who competes in the Men's Triathlon at 9pm tonight.

Khelan and Kwong also return to the pool for the 50m Backstroke events from 10pm tonight.
